problem: The direction of the core-size loss is stated backwards. Light from the smaller core (50 μm) falls entirely inside the larger core (62.5 μm), so with equal NA there is almost no core-size loss in the small-to-large direction; the chapter claims this direction 'loses the fraction outside the smaller core'. The reverse (62.5 μm into 50 μm) loss is geometric overlap, roughly the area ratio, not an angular effect: with equal NA the smaller fiber accepts all angles that the larger one emits.
fix: If the cores differ and the NAs are equal, the loss appears mainly when light goes from the larger core into the smaller one. The smaller core acts as a stop: with uniform (over-filled) launch the coupled fraction is about (a_small/a_large)², i.e. (50/62.5)² ≈ 0.64, about 1.9 dB going 62.5 μm → 50 μm. Going 50 μm → 62.5 μm the light enters the larger core fully and the core-size loss is negligible. Angular acceptance loss appears only when the NAs (acceptance angles) differ, not from core diameter alone.
